title: Sounding natural
goal: React the way Telugu speakers do, use tags, tone words and echo words, mix in English naturally, and keep a conversation going when you don't understand or don't know a word.
intro:
You can now say almost anything you need. This unit is about saying it **the way people actually talk**: the little noises a listener makes (**ఊ**, **హా**, **అలాగా?**), the exclamations (**అబ్బో!**, **వామ్మో!**, **ఛ!**), the tags that turn a statement into a nudge (**వస్తావు కదూ?** you'll come, won't you?; **చెప్పానుగా!** I told you, didn't I!), and tone words that soften or sharpen a sentence (**సరేలే**, **మాత్రం**, **అయినా**).

You'll also learn Telugu's playful **echo words** (*టీ గీ తాగుదామా?* 'shall we have tea or something?'), the English that young people mix in (*లైట్ తీసుకో*, *ఫీల్ అవ్వకు*, *చిల్ అవుతున్నా*), and, just as important, how to survive when you miss something: asking someone to repeat, to slow down, or to explain a word, and how to talk your way round a word you don't know.

grammar.title: Tag questions: కదా, కదూ, -గా, లేదా
grammar.body:
Telugu speakers constantly hang a little tag on the end of a sentence to pull the listener in. Each one has its own feel.

**కదా** (Unit 20), 'isn't it / right?': checks something you both know or expect. *రేపు సెలవు కదా?* (tomorrow's a holiday, right?) Polite: **కదండీ**.

**కదూ**, 'won't you? / didn't you?': softer, more personal, coaxing. Use it to ask a favour or extract a promise, *వస్తావు కదూ?* (you'll come, won't you?), or to gently accuse, *నువ్వే తిన్నావు కదూ?* (it was you who ate it, wasn't it?).

**-గా** stuck straight onto the verb or word: 'you know / didn't I?'. It points to something the listener already knows and is often a little impatient: *చెప్పానుగా!* (I told you, didn't I!), *తెలుసుగా* (you know, right), *వచ్చాడుగా* (he did come, you know).

**… లేదా?**, 'or not?': puts pressure on: *వస్తున్నావా లేదా?* (are you coming or not?). Polite and neutral: *-ఆ, లేదా?*

And any word can be echoed back with **-ఆ?** to show surprise (Unit 20): *నువ్వా?* (you?!), *ఇంతా?* (this much?!).

**The trap**: కదా and కదూ assume the answer is yes. To ask for information you don't have, use a plain -ఆ question: *మీరు తెలుగువాళ్ళా?*, not *మీరు తెలుగువాళ్ళు కదా?* (which means 'you're Telugu, aren't you?').

examples.en: You'll come to the party, won't you?
I told you there'd be traffic, didn't I!
It was you who ate my chocolate, wasn't it?

grammar.title: Little words that set the tone: -ఏ, -ఓ, -లే, మాత్రం, అయినా
grammar.body:
Small particles do a lot of the emotional work in Telugu. You know some already; here they are side by side.

**-ఏ** (Unit 26), 'the very, just, -self': points at one thing and no other. *నువ్వే చెప్పు* (you tell me), *ఇప్పుడే* (right now), *అదే* (that very one).

**-ఓ**, vagueness, 'some-/-ever' and 'or': *ఎవరో* (someone), *ఏదో* (something or other), *ఎక్కడో* (somewhere), *ఏదో ఒకటి* (anything at all), *టీయో కాఫీయో* (tea or coffee, whichever). In Unit 37 it also made embedded questions.

**-లే**, a shrug: softens, reassures, or closes the subject. *సరేలే* (fine then), *పోనీలే* (never mind), *వస్తాలే* (I'll come, relax), *పర్వాలేదులే* (it's fine). Said too often it sounds offhand.

**మాత్రం**, contrast: 'as for X / X though / X at least'. It goes right after the word it contrasts: *అందరూ వచ్చారు, వాడు మాత్రం రాలేదు* (everyone came; he didn't, though) · *నువ్వు మాత్రం రావాలి* (you, at least, have to come).

**అయినా** at the start of a sentence, 'anyway, after all, in any case': it changes the angle or dismisses: *అయినా నీకెందుకు?* (anyway, why do you care?). (After a verb, -ఇనా still means 'even if', Unit 19.)

**The trap**: -ఏ and మాత్రం can both come out as 'only' in English. -ఏ picks one out (*ఇదే కావాలి*, I want *this one*); మాత్రం sets it against the rest (*ఇది మాత్రం వద్దు*, not this one, though).

examples.en: You tell me, what should I do?
Someone called; they didn't give a name.
Fine, I'll let it go this time.

examples.native: అయినా ఇంత రాత్రి ఎందుకు ఫోన్ చేశావు?
examples.roman: ayinā inta rātri enduku phōn chēshāvu?
examples.en: Anyway, why did you call so late at night?

grammar.title: Echo words: టీ గీ, పార్టీ గీర్టీ
grammar.body:
Telugu has a playful way of saying 'X or something / X and all that': repeat the word with its **first syllable replaced by గి-** (or **గీ-** if that syllable's vowel is long). The rest of the word stays the same:
టీ → **టీ గీ** · కాఫీ → **కాఫీ గీఫీ** · సినిమా → **సినిమా గినిమా** · పార్టీ → **పార్టీ గీర్టీ** · పెళ్ళి → **పెళ్ళి గిళ్ళి** · డబ్బులు → **డబ్బులు గిబ్బులు** · సారీ → **సారీ గీరీ** · షాపింగ్ → **షాపింగ్ గీపింగ్**

**What it does**
• casual vagueness: *టీ గీ తాగుదామా?* (shall we grab a tea or something?)
• with a negative, it waves the whole thing away: *పెళ్ళి గిళ్ళి ఏమీ లేదు* (no wedding, nothing of the sort) · *సారీ గీరీ వద్దు* (spare me the sorry)

**Other doublings** you already hear everywhere: for intensity, *చిన్న చిన్న* (tiny little), *వేడివేడిగా* (piping hot, Unit 24); for 'each, which ones', *ఎవరెవరు* (who all, Unit 21); for urgency, a doubled command, *చెప్పు చెప్పు* (go on, tell me), *రా రా* (come in, come in), *ఆగాగు* (wait, wait).

**The trap**: echo words are strictly informal and slightly cheeky. Use them with friends and family, never with your boss or a stranger: *మీటింగ్ గీటింగ్* to a manager sounds as if you don't take it seriously.

examples.en: Shall we have a tea or something this evening?

examples.native: పార్టీ గీర్టీ ఏమీ వద్దు, ఇంట్లోనే ఉందాం.
examples.roman: pārṭī gīrṭī ēmī vaddu, iṇṭlōnē undām.
examples.en: No party or anything; let's just stay home.
Don't give me sorry and all that; just don't do it again.

examples.native: పెళ్ళి గిళ్ళి ఏమీ లేదు, ఇప్పుడే ఉద్యోగంలో చేరాను.
examples.roman: peḷḷi giḷḷi ēmī lēdu, ippuḍē udyōgamlō chērānu.
examples.en: No wedding or anything like that; I've only just started work.
Go on, tell me, what happened next?

dialogue.title: Mastu
dialogue.setting: Hyderabad. Emma, who has been learning Telugu for a year, meets her friend Pavan's cousin Srikanth, visiting from Warangal.

lines.speaker: Pavan
lines.native: ఎమ్మా, ఇతను మా కజిన్ శ్రీకాంత్. వరంగల్ నుంచి వచ్చాడు.
lines.roman: emmā, itanu mā kajin shrīkānt. varaṅgal nunchi vachchāḍu.
lines.en: Emma, this is my cousin Srikanth. He's come from Warangal.

lines.speaker: Srikanth
lines.en: Hi! What are you doing in Hyderabad? (Telangana dialect)

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.en: Sorry, could you say that again? A bit slower...

lines.speaker: Pavan
lines.native: హహ, వాడిది తెలంగాణ యాస. "హైదరాబాద్‌లో ఏం చేస్తున్నావు?" అని అడుగుతున్నాడు.
lines.roman: haha, vāḍidi telaṅgāṇa yāsa. "haidarābādlō ēm chēstunnāvu?" ani aḍugutunnāḍu.
lines.en: Ha ha, that's his Telangana accent. He's asking, 'What are you doing in Hyderabad?'

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: ఓహో, అలాగా! నేను ఇక్కడ ఒక కంపెనీలో పని చేస్తున్నా. తెలుగు కూడా నేర్చుకుంటున్నా.
lines.roman: ōhō, alāgā! nēnu ikkaḍa oka kampenīlō pani chēstunnā. telugu kūḍā nērchukuṇṭunnā.
lines.en: Oh, I see! I work at a company here. And I'm learning Telugu.

lines.speaker: Srikanth
lines.en: Wow! You speak Telugu really well!

lines.speaker: Pavan
lines.native: "చాలా" అని. హైదరాబాద్‌లో అందరూ అంటారు: మస్తు బాగుంది, మస్తు ట్రాఫిక్...
lines.roman: "chālā" ani. haidarābādlō andarū aṇṭāru: mastu bāgundi, mastu ṭrāphik...
lines.en: It means 'very'. Everyone in Hyderabad says it: mastu good, mastu traffic...

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: సూపర్! ఇంకోటి... అదే, ఏమంటారు... రోడ్డు మీద తినే చిన్న చిన్న వడలు...
lines.roman: sūpar! iṅkōṭi... adē, ēmaṇṭāru... rōḍḍu mīda tinē chinna chinna vaḍalu...
lines.en: Great! One more thing... those, what are they called... the tiny little vadas you eat on the street...

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: అదీ! పునుగులు! నాకు అవి మస్తు ఇష్టం!
lines.roman: adī! punugulu! nāku avi mastu iṣṭam!
lines.en: That's it! Punugulu! I love them mastu!

lines.speaker: Srikanth
lines.native: అదరగొట్టేశావ్! పదండి, ఇప్పుడే పునుగులు గినుగులు తిందాం.
lines.roman: adaragoṭṭēshāv! padaṇḍi, ippuḍē punugulu ginugulu tindām.
lines.en: You nailed it! Come on, let's go and have some punugulu or whatever right now.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.native: సరేలే, కానీ ఈసారి బిల్లు మాత్రం నాది, సరేనా?
lines.roman: sarēlē, kānī īsāri billu mātram nādi, sarēnā?
lines.en: All right, but this time the bill is mine, OK?

lines.speaker: Pavan
lines.native: అయినా నువ్వు మా గెస్ట్ కదా. ఛ, అది కుదరదు!
lines.roman: ayinā nuvvu mā gesṭ kadā. chha, adi kudaradu!
lines.en: Come on, you're our guest, aren't you? No way, that's not happening!

culture: Telugu has strong regional **యాస** (accents and dialects), and people love to tease each other about them. **Telangana** speech, including much of Hyderabad, says *ఏంది* for *ఏంటి*, *ఎట్లా* for *ఎలా*, *జేస్తున్నవ్* for *చేస్తున్నావు*, *-ల* for *-లో* (*ఇంట్ల*, at home) and *మస్తు* for *చాలా*, with plenty of Hindi-Urdu words; the old city's Dakhni Hindi adds *క్యా బే* to the mix. **Coastal Andhra**, especially the Godavari districts, is known for a sing-song, very polite style full of *-అండీ*; **Rayalaseema** has its own sound and words. The standard you've learnt is understood everywhere, and people will happily switch to it for you. Everyday speech is also full of English (**Tenglish**): *లైట్ తీసుకో*, *ఫీల్ అవ్వకు*, *టెన్షన్ పడకు*, *క్లారిటీ లేదు*, *సెట్ అయింది*. The trick is to keep the Telugu verb: English word + *చేయు / అవు / పడు / తీసుకో*. Listeners are expected to make noise (*ఊ*, *హా*, *అవునా?*); silence sounds like you're not interested. And if you're learning, say so: *నాకు తెలుగు ఇంకా అంత బాగా రాదు* gets you patience, praise and, usually, a snack.

tip.title: React out loud
tip.body:
- While someone talks: **ఊ**, **హా**, **అలాగా?** (I see), **ఓహో** (oh, I get it).
- Impressed: **అబ్బో!** · shocked: **వామ్మో!** · annoyed: **ఛ!**
- Brushing it off: **అబ్బే** (nah, not at all).
- Tone matters: a flat అబ్బో can be sarcastic.

sentences.en: Uh-huh, and then?
Yeah, coming!
Is that so? I didn't know.
Oh, I see, so that's why you didn't come!
Ooh, a new bike! When did you buy it?
Oh my god, so much traffic!
Damn, I missed the bus!
Nah, I'm not angry.

sentences.native: అబ్బే, అలాంటిదేమీ లేదు, మేము ఫ్రెండ్స్ అంతే.
sentences.roman: abbē, alāṇṭidēmī lēdu, mēmu phreṇḍs antē.
sentences.en: Nah, nothing like that; we're just friends.

tip.title: Tags: కదా, కదూ, -గా, లేదా
tip.body:
- **కదా?** right? (you both know it): *రేపు సెలవు కదా?*
- **కదూ?** softer, coaxing: *వస్తావు కదూ?* (you'll come, won't you?)
- **-గా** on the verb = 'I told you / you know': *చెప్పానుగా!*
- **…లేదా?** impatient 'or not?': *వస్తున్నావా లేదా?*

sentences.native: నువ్వు ఈరోజు ఫ్రీ కదా? మనం సినిమాకి వెళ్దాం.
sentences.roman: nuvvu īrōju phrī kadā? manam sinimāki veḷdām.
sentences.en: You're free today, right? Let's go to a film.

sentences.native: నాకోసం ఒక చిన్న పని చేస్తావు కదూ?
sentences.roman: nākōsam oka chinna pani chēstāvu kadū?
sentences.en: You'll do a little something for me, won't you?

sentences.native: మా ఇంటికి రేపు భోజనానికి వస్తావు కదూ?
sentences.roman: mā iṇṭiki rēpu bhōjanāniki vastāvu kadū?
sentences.en: You'll come over for a meal tomorrow, won't you?

sentences.native: నేను ముందే చెప్పానుగా, ఆ హోటల్ బాగోదని!
sentences.roman: nēnu mundē cheppānugā, ā hōṭal bāgōdani!
sentences.en: I told you that restaurant was no good, didn't I!
You know I can't take spicy food.
Are you coming or not? Everyone's waiting.
It was you who ate my biryani, wasn't it?

sentences.native: ఆగాగు, నువ్వు నిన్న అక్కడే ఉన్నావు కదా?
sentences.roman: āgāgu, nuvvu ninna akkaḍē unnāvu kadā?
sentences.en: Wait, wait, you were right there yesterday, weren't you?

sentences.native: అదీ సంగతి! అందుకే వాడు ఫోన్ ఎత్తట్లేదు.
sentences.roman: adī saṅgati! andukē vāḍu phōn ettaṭlēdu.
sentences.en: So that's what it is! That's why he isn't answering.
That's it, now you're talking!

tip.title: Tone words: -లే, మాత్రం, అయినా, -ఓ
tip.body:
- **-లే** softens or shrugs: **సరేలే** (fine then), **వస్తాలే** (I'll come, relax).
- **మాత్రం** = as for X / X though: క్లైమాక్స్ **మాత్రం** సూపర్.
- **అయినా** at the start = anyway, after all.
- **-ఓ** = some-/-ever: **ఏదో**, **ఎవరో**; **-ఏ** = the very one: **నువ్వే**.

sentences.en: Fine, let's do it your way.
Don't panic, I'll be there.
Everyone laughed; she didn't, though.

sentences.native: సినిమా బోరింగ్, కానీ క్లైమాక్స్ మాత్రం సూపర్.
sentences.roman: sinimā bōriṅg, kānī klaimāks mātram sūpar.
sentences.en: The film was boring, but the climax, though, was great.

sentences.native: అయినా అది నీ సమస్య కాదు, లైట్ తీసుకో.
sentences.roman: ayinā adi nī samasya kādu, laiṭ tīsukō.
sentences.en: Anyway, it's not your problem; don't sweat it.

sentences.native: ఏదో ఒకటి తిందాం, నాకు ఆకలిగా ఉంది.
sentences.roman: ēdō okaṭi tindām, nāku ākaligā undi.
sentences.en: Let's eat something, anything; I'm hungry.

sentences.native: నేను ఏమీ అనలేదు, నువ్వే ఫీల్ అయ్యావు.
sentences.roman: nēnu ēmī analēdu, nuvvē phīl ayyāvu.
sentences.en: I didn't say anything; you're the one who got upset.

sentences.native: అయినా ఇంత చిన్న విషయానికి అంత టెన్షన్ ఎందుకు?
sentences.roman: ayinā inta chinna viṣayāniki anta ṭenṣan enduku?
sentences.en: After all, why get so stressed over such a small thing?

sentences.native: వాడి మాటలకి ఫీల్ అవ్వకు, వాడు అంతే.
sentences.roman: vāḍi māṭalaki phīl avvaku, vāḍu antē.
sentences.en: Don't take what he says to heart, he's just like that.

sentences.native: పరీక్ష అయిపోయింది కదా, ఇక లైట్ తీసుకో.
sentences.roman: parīkṣa ayipōyindi kadā, ika laiṭ tīsukō.
sentences.en: The exam's over, right? Now take it easy.

tip.title: Echo words: టీ గీ, పార్టీ గీర్టీ
tip.body:
- Repeat the word with its first syllable changed to **గి-** (**గీ-** if the vowel is long): సినిమా **గినిమా**, టీ **గీ**, పార్టీ **గీర్టీ**.
- Meaning: 'X or something / X and all that'.
- With a negative it waves it away: పెళ్ళి **గిళ్ళి** ఏమీ లేదు.
- Strictly informal: never to your boss.

sentences.en: Shall we have a coffee or something this evening?

sentences.native: డబ్బులు గిబ్బులు ఏమీ వద్దు, ఫ్రెండ్ కోసం చేస్తా.
sentences.roman: ḍabbulu gibbulu ēmī vaddu, phreṇḍ kōsam chēstā.
sentences.en: I don't want money or anything; I'll do it for a friend.

sentences.native: ఈ వీకెండ్ సినిమా గినిమా ఏమైనా ఉందా?
sentences.roman: ī vīkeṇḍ sinimā ginimā ēmainā undā?
sentences.en: Any film or anything this weekend?
Are you throwing a birthday party or anything?

sentences.native: పరీక్షలు గిరీక్షలు అయిపోయాయి, ఇప్పుడు చిల్ అవుతున్నా.
sentences.roman: parīkṣalu girīkṣalu ayipōyāyi, ippuḍu chil avutunnā.
sentences.en: Exams and all that are over; now I'm chilling.

sentences.native: షాపింగ్ గీపింగ్ ఏమీ లేదు, ఇంట్లోనే చిల్ అవుతున్నా.
sentences.roman: ṣāpiṅg gīpiṅg ēmī lēdu, iṇṭlōnē chil avutunnā.
sentences.en: No shopping or anything; I'm just chilling at home.
Spare me the sorry; I'll let it go this time.
Come on, let's chill at the beach with the gang.
There's no clarity on the plan yet.
You nailed it in yesterday's presentation!

lessons.title: When you didn't catch it

tip.title: Didn't catch that?
tip.body:
- Didn't hear: **ఏమన్నావు?** (informal) / **ఏమన్నారు?** (polite).
- Ask again with **-తారా?**: **ఇంకోసారి చెప్తారా?** · **స్లోగా మాట్లాడతారా?**
- Say where you're at: **నాకు తెలుగు ఇంకా అంత బాగా రాదు**; people slow down at once.

new: నాకు తెలుగు ఇంకా అంత బాగా రాదు.

sentences.en: Sorry, what did you say? I didn't catch it.
What did you say? It's too loud, I can't hear.
Could you repeat that?

sentences.native: మీరు చాలా తొందరగా మాట్లాడుతున్నారు, కొంచెం నెమ్మదిగా.
sentences.roman: mīru chālā tondaragā māṭlāḍutunnāru, konchem nemmadigā.
sentences.en: You're speaking very fast; a bit slower, please.

sentences.native: నాకు తెలుగు కొంచెం కొంచెం వచ్చు, అంత బాగా రాదు.
sentences.roman: nāku telugu konchem konchem vachchu, anta bāgā rādu.
sentences.en: I know a little Telugu, not very well.
Is my pronunciation right?

sentences.native: నీ ఉచ్చారణ చాలా బాగుంది, తెలుగువాళ్ళ లాగే ఉంది!
sentences.roman: nī uchchāraṇa chālā bāgundi, teluguvāḷḷa lāgē undi!
sentences.en: Your pronunciation is really good, just like a Telugu speaker's!
The Godavari accent is lovely to listen to.

sentences.native: ఆయన యాస నాకు అస్సలు అర్థం కాలేదు.
sentences.roman: āyana yāsa nāku assalu artham kālēdu.
sentences.en: I didn't understand his accent at all.

lessons.title: Talking round a word you don't know

tip.title: Talking round a word
tip.body:
- Ask: **X అంటే ఏంటి?** · **తెలుగులో దీన్ని ఏమంటారు?**
- Stall while you search: **అదే... ఏమంటారు...**
- Describe it with a relative clause: *రోడ్డు మీద అమ్మే చిన్న వడలు* 'the little vadas they sell on the street'.
- Got it? **అదీ!** (that's it!)

sentences.en: What does "mastu" mean?
What's this word in English?
In Telugu this is called a "kuḷāyi".

sentences.native: ఈ పదం నాకు కొత్త, కొంచెం వివరిస్తారా?
sentences.roman: ī padam nāku kotta, konchem vivaristārā?
sentences.en: This word is new to me; could you explain it a bit?
If you give me an example, I'll get it.
For example, "super" means "really good".

sentences.native: అదే, ఏమంటారు, పుట్టినరోజుకి కట్ చేసేది... ఆ, కేక్!
sentences.roman: adē, ēmaṇṭāru, puṭṭinarōjuki kaṭ chēsēdi... ā, kēk!
sentences.en: That... what's it called... the thing you cut on birthdays... ah, cake!

sentences.native: రోడ్డు మీద అమ్మే చిన్న చిన్న వడలు ఉంటాయి కదా, వాటిని ఏమంటారు?
sentences.roman: rōḍḍu mīda ammē chinna chinna vaḍalu uṇṭāyi kadā, vāṭini ēmaṇṭāru?
sentences.en: You know those tiny vadas they sell on the street? What are they called?
In Hyderabad everyone says mastu.
That's it! That's the word I was looking for.
